content.page_title: Management of non-IRA revascularization and evaluation of non-infarct-related artery stenosis severity

10.3.2 Patients presenting with non-ST-e.summary: There are fewer data guiding management of patients presenting with NSTE-ACS and multivessel disease (MVD) compared with STEMI/MVD. No dedicated randomized trial comparing complete revascularization vs IRA-only PCI for these patients exists. Observational studies and meta-analyses of non-randomized studies suggest complete revascularization is associated with fewer deaths and MACE vs IRA-only PCI, but results are hypothesis-generating given non-randomized data.
key_points: Lack of dedicated randomized trials comparing complete revascularization vs IRA-only PCI for NSTE-ACS with MVD.
Observational/meta-analytic evidence suggests fewer deaths and MACE with complete revascularization versus IRA-only PCI, but evidence is limited by non-randomized study designs.

10.4 Evaluation of non-infarct-related a.summary: Quantitative coronary angiography may overestimate severity of non-IRA lesions compared with repeat angiography. Microvascular constriction can affect functional measurements; FFR use can change management decisions and guide PCI in multivessel disease. Trial and registry data provide specific proportions and outcomes related to FFR-guided assessment.
key_points: Overestimation of non-IRA lesion severity by single angiography compared with repeat angiogram within 9 months has been reported.
Microvascular constriction in non-IRAs may cause variation between baseline and follow-up functional measurements.
Sub-analysis of FAME: 65% of lesions in the angiographic 50–70% diameter stenosis range had an FFR >0.80; 20% of lesions in the 71–90% range had an FFR >0.80.

PRIME-FFR registry included 533 ACS patients: systematic FFR measurement led to a change in management strategy in 38% of cases (e.g., CABG→PCI or medical treatment) without impact on MACE, death/MI, or angina symptoms at 1 year.

Subgroup analysis of FAME in 328 ACS patients (UA or NSTEMI) with MVD: adoption of FFR to guide PCI resulted in similar risk reductions of MACE compared with patients with stable angina, with fewer stents implanted and less contrast media use.

FAMOUS-NSTEMI randomized 350 patients with NSTE-ACS and ≥1 coronary stenosis (>30%) to angiography-guided vs FFR-guided management and found a higher proportion of patients in the FFR-guided group were initially treated with medical therapy.

PRIME_FFR_registry.follow_up_outcomes_impact: no impact on MACE, death/MI, or angina at 1 year

FAME_subgroup.finding: FFR-guided PCI had similar MACE risk reductions as in stable angina, fewer stents and less contrast use

FAMOUS_NSTEMI.finding: Higher proportion initially treated with medical therapy in FFR-guided arm

content.other_notes: No surgical studies have specifically investigated non-IRA revascularization. Given inadequate randomized evidence on optimal timing (immediate vs staged) of non-IRA PCI, no recommendation can be formulated for immediate vs staged non-IRA PCI.
